questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for LEA eligibility under RA 9266, Section 13?

options.text: Bachelor of Science in Architecture from CHED-accredited school
Minimum 3 years of work experience in a construction company
Good moral character verified by NBI clearance
Diversified Architectural Experience of at least 2 years

rationale.a: This IS a requirement under RA 9266 Section 13; all candidates must hold a Bachelor of Science in Architecture from CHED-accredited institutions.
rationale.c: This IS a requirement; applicants must establish good moral character through NBI clearance and documentary evidence.
rationale.d: This IS a requirement; 2 years of diversified architectural experience (3,840 hours) is mandatory unless reduced by a Master's degree.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 Section 13 requires CHED-accredited Architecture degree + at least 2 years (3,840 hours) DAE. Good moral character is a general PRC exam requirement (not Sec 13-specific). No minimum work experience in construction companies is mandated.
rationale.takeaway: ALE eligibility requires CHED degree + good moral character + 2 years DAE (3,840 hours) — not 3 years of construction company employment.

questions.text: How do the academic and experiential pathways specified in RA 9266, Section 13 ensure that LEA candidates possess both theoretical and practical architectural competence?

options.text: By requiring a degree from CHED-accredited institutions and mandatory real-world DAE spanning multiple project phases
By accepting either a degree or professional experience, whichever is easier to acquire, which may not ensure comprehensive competence
By allowing alternative credentials from foreign universities without DAE verification, which could lead to inconsistencies in candidate preparedness
By focusing solely on written examination performance without regard to background, potentially overlooking practical skills

rationale.b: Contradicts the law; both pathways are mandatory, not alternative options. A degree without DAE or vice versa does not satisfy Section 13.
rationale.c: Falsely claims foreign credentials bypass DAE requirements; RA 9266 requires CHED-accredited degrees and mandatory experiential verification regardless of origin.
rationale.d: Diminishes the role of credentials; the ALE requires verified academic and experiential foundations, not examination performance in isolation.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 Section 13 requires both: (1) a five-year Bachelor of Science from CHED-accredited institutions (ensuring rigorous theoretical foundation) and (2) 2 years of diversified architectural experience spanning multiple project phases (ensuring practical competence). Neither requirement alone is sufficient.
rationale.takeaway: ALE eligibility combines academic rigor (CHED degree) + real-world breadth (2-year DAE across design, construction, site analysis) to ensure both theory and practice.

questions.text: An architect-mentor's Professional Tax Receipt expires during a candidate's DAE documentation period. How does this affect the candidate's eligibility for the LEA?

options.text: It has no effect if the mentor was registered when the DAE began
The candidate may still apply if the mentor's PTR is renewed before submission
The entire DAE period becomes invalid and must be redone
The Board will accept the application but with a provisional certificate pending mentor verification

rationale.a: Misinterprets continuity; mentor registration at the start does not excuse expiration of the PTR at application time, which is when the Board verifies credentials.
rationale.c: Overstates the consequence; renewal of the PTR cures the documentation gap without invalidating the completed DAE hours.
rationale.d: The Board does not issue provisional certificates pending mentor verification; credentials must be in order before registration is finalized.
rationale.correct: The source document requires the architect-mentor's Professional Tax Receipt as supporting documentation. Mentor's PTR must be current at application; hours under expired PTR may not qualify unless mentor renewed continuously.ials at the time of ALE application.
rationale.takeaway: Mentor's PTR expiration: candidate can still qualify if the PTR is renewed before ALE application submission.

questions.text: A candidate holding a Master's degree in Architecture from a CHED-accredited university applies for the LEA. By how many years is the standard DAE requirement reduced?

options.text: No reduction applies
6 months reduction
1 year reduction
2 years reduction

rationale.a: Incorrectly assumes no advantage for advanced postgraduate study; the law recognizes advanced coursework by reducing the experiential requirement.
rationale.b: Understates the benefit; the law provides a full 1-year reduction, not a 6-month reduction.
rationale.d: Confuses the overall requirement; eliminating the entire 2-year DAE would bypass the experiential foundation mandated by RA 9266.
rationale.correct: RRA 9266 Section 13 (as implemented) credits 1 year (1,920 hours) of Master's toward the at least 3,840-hour DAE total, requiring additional 1,920 practical hours.s with a government-recognized Master's degree in Architecture, leaving only 1 year (1,920 hours) of mandatory experience.
rationale.takeaway: Master's degree in Architecture from CHED-accredited institution = 1 year DAE credit (1,920 hours instead of 3,840).

questions.text: A candidate presents a Master's degree in Architecture from a private university claiming 1-year DAE credit. What is the Board's responsibility before accepting this claim?

options.text: Accept it automatically based on the degree level, assuming all Master's programs meet the same standards
Verify the university's CHED accreditation status before confirming the 1-year reduction
Require the candidate to complete the full 2-year DAE regardless of advanced degree, ensuring uniformity in qualification standards
Conduct an interview to assess the candidate's theoretical knowledge, focusing on the depth and relevance of their academic experience

rationale.a: Confuses degree level with institutional accreditation; the law requires a CHED-accredited institution, not merely a Master's-level degree.
rationale.c: Ignores the statutory reduction; a CHED-accredited Master's does qualify for the 1-year credit, but accreditation must first be verified.
rationale.d: Substitutes credentials verification with subjective knowledge assessment; the Board's role is to verify institutional accreditation, not interview candidates.
rationale.correct: The 1-year DAE reduction applies only to Master's degrees from 'government-recognized institutions' with CHED accreditation status. The Board must verify accreditation before granting the reduction; a private institution without CHED accreditation does not qualify.
rationale.takeaway: Master's degree DAE credit: Board must verify CHED accreditation status before confirming the 1-year reduction.

questions.text: What is the minimum cumulative hour requirement for Diversified Architectural Experience (DAE)?

options.text: 1,920 hours
3,840 hours
2,560 hours
4,000 hours

rationale.c: States an intermediate figure that matches neither the standard requirement (3,840 hours) nor the Master's-degree reduction (1,920 hours).
rationale.d: Overstates the requirement; the law specifies exactly 3,840 hours, not 4,000.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 Section 13 mandates exactly 3,840 cumulative hours of DAE (approximately 24 hours per week over 2 years) before exam eligibility.
rationale.takeaway: DAE requires 3,840 hours (2 years at ~24 hours/week) for all candidates without a Master's degree. PRC Board Resolution No. 09 requires at least an aggregate of 3,840 cumulative hours of DAE (RA 9266 Section 13 as amended by IRR). Master's provides 1-year (1,920-hour) credit toward the at least 3,840-hour total.

questions.text: A candidate completed her Bachelor's degree in Architecture in June 2023 and accumulated 3,840 hours of DAE by June 2025. When may she apply for the LEA?

options.text: Immediately upon graduation in June 2023, which is not possible as DAE requirements are not yet met
Only after June 2025, when the DAE requirement is satisfied
Six months before completing the DAE requirement, which is not allowed under current regulations
At any time, provided the NBI clearance is current, which overlooks the DAE requirement

rationale.a: Confuses graduation timing with DAE eligibility; a degree alone does not satisfy the 2-year experiential requirement.
rationale.c: Assumes early application is permitted; the law requires full completion of DAE, not early submission before hours accumulate.
rationale.d: Overestimates the flexibility; NBI clearance currency is necessary but not sufficient — DAE completion remains mandatory.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 Section 13 mandates that candidates must complete all 3,840 hours of DAE before applying for the ALE; the requirement is not negotiable.
rationale.takeaway: ALE application timing: only after completing all required DAE hours (3,840), not before.

questions.text: According to RA 9266, what consequence results from submitting false evidence or misrepresentations in an LEA application?

options.text: Fine of 50,000 pesos, which serves as a deterrent against fraudulent activities
Denial of registration or suspension/revocation of Certificate of Registration
One-year ban from reapplying, effectively delaying the applicant's professional progress
Mandatory completion of additional coursework, aimed at reinforcing ethical standards

rationale.a: While penalties may exist, the primary consequences stated in RA 9266 are denial/revocation, not a specific monetary fine.
rationale.c: The law does not specify a one-year reapplication ban; the focus is on denial of the current application and potential revocation.
rationale.d: Fraudulent conduct triggers denial or revocation, not mandatory coursework; additional education would not remedy dishonesty in the application process.
rationale.correct: RA 9266 states that fraudulent applications containing false evidence or misrepresentations result in denial of registration or, if discovered later, suspension or revocation of the Certificate of Registration.
rationale.takeaway: Fraud in ALE applications leads to denial of registration or revocation of the architect's Certificate of Registration.

questions.text: Diversified Architectural Experience must demonstrate variation across different phases and types of architectural service. Which scenario BEST illustrates compliance with this variation requirement?

options.text: Working 3,840 hours exclusively on building design under one architect-mentor, without exposure to other phases or types of projects
Experience spanning schematic design, construction administration, site analysis, and post-occupancy evaluation under different projects
Completing all 3,840 hours within the office of a large architectural firm, focusing solely on design development
Working solely on renovation and restoration projects for a single contractor, without involvement in new construction or other project types

rationale.a: Violates the variation requirement; limiting all 3,840 hours to building design alone fails to demonstrate competence across multiple architectural phases.
rationale.c: While an architectural firm may offer diverse work, this option doesn't specify whether the candidate actually worked across varied phases or concentrated in one area.
rationale.d: Confuses DAE with contractor-specific work; limiting experience to only renovation/restoration projects fails to demonstrate the required breadth across design, planning, and construction administration.
rationale.correct: DAE must demonstrate variation across different phases and types of architectural service, not concentration in a single area. Option b spans multiple design phases (schematic design, construction administration, site analysis, post-occupancy evaluation).
rationale.takeaway: DAE variation requirement: exposure to multiple project phases (design, construction administration, site analysis) — not concentration in one area.

questions.text: What document must be submitted to verify that a candidate's architect-mentor holds a valid Professional Identification Card?

options.text: Photocopy of the mentor's Professional Identification Card
Affidavit from the Board of Architecture, which is not typically required for this verification
Certificate from CHED confirming the mentor's credentials, which is not applicable for verifying a Professional Identification Card
Board Resolution authorizing the mentor's practice, which is not a standard document for this purpose

rationale.b: An affidavit from the Board is not required to verify the mentor's PIC; a direct photocopy of the valid ID serves as the primary proof.
rationale.c: CHED does not issue certificates confirming individual architect credentials; CHED accredits schools, not practicing professionals.
rationale.d: A Board Resolution is not necessary for verifying an individual mentor's Professional Identification Card; the card itself is the standard documentation.
rationale.correct: PRC Board of Architects (PRBoA) DAE logbook guidelines require photocopy of mentor's valid Professional Identification Card (PRC ID) to verify licensure and verify the mentor's current licensure status.
rationale.takeaway: To verify mentor credentials, submit a photocopy of the mentor's valid Professional Identification Card.
